W5 (contrarian), after E025.
1. Correction. E024 and E025 ran on the E023 tip (9.0 epochs, 225 steps), not on E017. E025's time equals the tip's (6.20 s), and E024's 6.07 s is only −2%. So the 26 px middle phase saves about 2% of time and cost about 0.28 pp on seeds 0–2. That weakens my final-map-regime mechanism (3×3 vs 2×2): with 26 px still in the 3×3 regime, the regime idea predicted no cost. It favours a scale or adaptation explanation: features learned at low resolution have to re-adapt in the 32 px tail.
2. New mechanism nobody has proposed: stem miscalibration. The whitening filters are computed on 32 px images but are mostly applied to antialiased, downsampled 24/28 px images, whose 2×2 patch covariance is different. Worse, the whitening bias trains only for the first 3 epochs (75 steps), which all fall in the 24 px phase (the first 90 steps). It is then frozen through the 32 px tail, so it stays miscalibrated, and GELU follows the stem before any BN can correct it. This predicts:
   - Low-resolution cuts cost more than the pixel count suggests (E011, E018, E024 all fit).
   - Letting the whitening bias train again during the 32 px tail, or recomputing the whitening per resolution, is a time-neutral booster.
   - FreezeOut of the stem plus group 1 in the tail hurts more than expected, because it blocks exactly the re-adaptation the tail exists for.
3. Noise. A same-commit rebuild moves the 3-seed mean by about 0.05 pp. Any graph or RNG change is a fresh 3-seed draw (SD about 0.25 pp). My estimate of the tip's true mean is about 0.7545, so the margin over 0.753 is thin, roughly coin-flip plus.
4. Plateau. Weight decay, label smoothing and Muon lr all land between 0.7537 and 0.7557. Muon applies no wd and renormalizes the filters, so filter wd is inert. The averaging-ramp exponent of 2 (E025, +0.19 pp at the same time) is the only booster with a positive reading, and it was discarded only because time did not improve. It should be stacked with an epoch trim.
5. Epoch dial. About 25 ms per step plus about 0.4 s fixed. Each 0.25 epoch is about −0.15 s and about −0.12 pp. Larger batch: fewer steps likely cost accuracy, as with SGD, at a small time gain because the run is GPU-bound with CUDA graphs.
6. Throughput. I count about 0.45 GMAC per sample forward at 32 px, roughly 2.7 GFLOP for forward plus backward. Over 225 steps at the pixel mix that implies more than 100 TFLOP/s effective, so no kernel lever is left (H6 is likely false).
7. Time model. Time ≈ steps × (stem-output pixels) mix plus about 0.4 s. The 32 px tail is about 40% of training time.
Unsure: the held-out mean for E025's alpha²; whether my stem-bias mechanism is real (cheap to test); judge-GPU transfer.
Best path: alpha² plus −0.25 epoch, plus the whitening bias trainable again in the 32 px tail. Judge on 13 seeds.

forecasts.reason: No recipe change, so the measurement is a tip rerun. The FLOP count implies more than 100 TFLOP/s effective, which leaves little kernel headroom.
I038 was discarded, so branch (b) applies: −0.25 epoch, about −0.15 s and −0.12 pp from a thin true margin. It is a coin flip whether it clears both bars.
Freezing the stem and group 1 blocks the 32 px re-adaptation that the tail exists for, so I expect a loss of more than 0.2 pp. The time saving is about 4–5%.
About 11% fewer steps is roughly a −0.8 epoch cut. Loss-based selection with stale, augmented, mixed-resolution losses recovers little of that.
The run is GPU-bound with CUDA graphs, so 20% fewer steps saves only about 3% of time. Fewer Muon and Lookahead updates cost about 0.2–0.4 pp.
The Muon lr sits on a plateau. Renormalized filters make lr a pure angular step size, and doubling it is likely flat to slightly harmful.

cruxes: Is the stem miscalibrated? The whitening bias trains only during the first 75 steps (all at 24 px) and the whitening is computed at 32 px. If letting the whitening bias train again in the 32 px tail (or recomputing the whitening per resolution) adds ≥0.2 pp at the same time, low-resolution cuts become cheap again.
Does E025's alpha-exponent-2 averaging hold its +0.19 pp on held-out seeds 3–12? If so, alpha² plus −0.25 to −0.5 epoch is the best time move.
What is the tip's true held-out mean at 9.0 epochs (E023)? That number sets how much margin the epoch dial can spend.
